title: Bailing out: when React skips a subtree

slides.say: By default, a re-render re-renders every child. But React can bail out and skip a whole subtree.
Bailout one: setting state to an identical value. Bailout two: a memo component whose props are all equal by Object dot is.

slides.text: On a bailout, React skips the component and its children. It may still call the component once first.
slides.say: Then React skips re-rendering the component and its children. It may still need to call the component before skipping, which should not affect your code.

slides.text: Context changes still get through to readers.
slides.say: One exception: components reading a context still re-render when that context changes, even below a memo.
